title: How Long Will EU Countries Waste Police Resources On Cannabis While Belgium Becomes “A Narco State”?
description: For the last year or so, the European media have carried stories about how Belgium is becoming or has become a “Narco State.” A little background. ...
content_html_sanitized:
For the last year or so, the European media have carried stories about how Belgium is becoming or has become a “Narco State.”

 

A little background.

 

First, geography. Belgium's leading port is Antwerp, the second biggest port in Europe, after Rotterdam, and ahead of Hamburg, Germany.

 

Brussels, the capital of Belgium, is also the capital of the European Union, and the ultimate cosmopolitan center, with a population of about 1,250,000 that is only 22% Belgian, and 41.8% is non-European.

 

It is a perfect place to run an international criminal organization. On the other hand, it is a dangerous place to be a judge investigating those organizations.

 

The website, BrusselsSignal.eu reported yesterday, “Criminals have the upper hand in Belgium, according to an Antwerp-based judge.

The investigating judge, a woman, has written a damning letterto the Justice Committee about the emergence of a ‘narco state’ in Belgium, a country that is becoming synonymous with “dark money, corruption and violence”.

 

The judge, whose name was withheld, has herself had to hide in a safe house for four months after receiving threats from drugs criminals. Other judges face serious danger, she claimed in the letter to Antwerp Court of Appeal, published today.

 

On the other hand, Belgium is famous for its great restaurants, perfect for a gourmet gangster, with or without the munchies. However, that’s not the reason they are there.

 

Belgium is a “gateway” to Northern Europe, where

The European Union Drugs Agency report reflects the increasing health problems related to “hard drugs”, and the inevitable legalization of cannabis.

 

Very simply, Europe has a serious law enforcement problem as part of the international “Drug War”, and it is absurdly irresponsible to continue to waste finite law enforcement/criminal justice resources to keep cannabis in the same market with much more problematic substances.

See  KEY TREND 1: A liberal cannabis belt has emerged in western Europe, with Germany

at its centre.

 

Of course, I have to note that cannabis is “technically” illegal in Belgium, even though it is on the Netherlands’ southern border. So, in effect, Belgium has ceded control of its cannabis supply to Dutch retailers and its domestic black market. Given the absurdity of that situation, Belgian judges shouldn’t expect any relief anytime soon.

There is also large-scale illegal cannabis cultivation in Belgium.
